_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Solomon Islands covering Papuan settlement (~30,000 BCE, among earliest in Pacific), Austronesian arrival (~4000 BCE), Lapita expansion, Alvaro de Mendaña 'discovery' 1568 (named after King Solomon, believed gold), headhunting/warrior culture, British Solomon Islands Protectorate (1893), WWII (Battle of Guadalcanal 1942-43, decisive Pacific campaign, Henderson Field, 'The Slot'), Maasina Rule movement, independence 1978, ethnic tensions (1998-2003, RAMSI intervention), China diplomatic switch 2019.

religion.note: Church of Melanesia (Anglican, 31.9%, Melanesian Brotherhood monastic order unique); South Seas Evangelical Church (17.1%, American SSEM missionaries); Seventh-day Adventist (11.2%); United Church (10.3%); Catholic (~20%); Christianity deeply embedded, replaced traditional worship but kastom (custom) practices persist alongside; church primary institution in rural areas; cargo cult influences (John Frum movement influence from Vanuatu)

ethnic_groups.name: Melanesian
ethnic_groups.notes: Diverse Melanesian peoples; 74 languages; wantok system (kinship obligation); kastom (traditional customs, land tenure, dispute resolution); headhunting historically practiced (ended early 20th century, skull houses preserved/tourist sites); betel nut universal; shell money (strings of shell discs, still used for bride price/traditional transactions, parallel economy); Big Man system (achieved status, not hereditary like Polynesian chiefs); subsistence gardening (sweet potato, taro, yam); canoe culture

ethnic_groups.name: Polynesian
ethnic_groups.notes: Polynesian outliers: Rennell and Bellona (~3k, distinct Polynesian culture in Melanesian sea, East Rennellese UNESCO); Ontong Java; Tikopia (~1.2k, studied by Raymond Firth, population control, unique society); Sikaiana; Anuta (smallest Polynesian society, ~300 people)

ethnic_groups.name: Micronesian
ethnic_groups.notes: Gilbertese settlers (relocated from overpopulated Gilbert Islands during British administration); small communities

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~2k, targeted in 2006 Chinatown riots Honiara, business community, resentment); European/Australian (mining, logging, aid workers); Bougainvillean (refugees, shared culture with western Solomons)

country_profile.notes_unique: Battle of Guadalcanal (August 1942 - February 1943, first major Allied offensive Pacific Theatre, US Marines vs Japanese, Henderson Field airstrip, 'The Slot' naval battles, Tokyo Express, 7,100 US/31,000 Japanese dead, turning point of Pacific War, Iron Bottom Sound 50+ ships from both sides sunk, WWII relics tourism); ethnic tensions/civil war (1998-2003, 'The Tensions', Guadalcanal vs Malaitan migrants, Isatabu Freedom Movement ethnic cleansing of Malaitans, Malaita Eagle Force retaliated, government collapsed, 200+ killed, 35k+ displaced, gun culture); RAMSI (Regional Assistance Mission to Solomon Islands 2003-2017, Australian-led Pacific Islands Forum peacekeeping, restored order, rebuilt police/institutions, successful intervention, largest Pacific security operation since WWII); China switch (September 2019, switched diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China/PRC, most significant Pacific diplomacy shift, Chinese money/infrastructure, Malaita Province refused to accept, pro-Taiwan, Sogavare centralised power); 2021 Honiara riots (November, anti-Sogavare protests, Chinatown burned, Australian troops deployed, 3 dead, China switch backlash, Malaita tensions); shell money (red-feather money from Santa Cruz, shell strings, traditional bride price, customary land transactions, parallel economy); logging (massive, Malaysian/Chinese companies, deforestation, unsustainable, corruption, 60%+ government revenue); customary land (87% communal/tribal ownership, development obstacle, disputes); Mendaña named islands 1568 (believed gold, named after King Solomon); Kennedy Island (JFK PT-109 sunk 1943, rescued by Solomon Islanders, future US president); Melanesian Brotherhood (Anglican monastic order, unique, peace missions during Tensions); East Rennell (UNESCO, largest raised coral atoll lake in world); extremely low development (one of poorest Pacific states)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Jeremiah Manele
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Independent/OUR Party; former Foreign Minister; succeeded Sogavare after 2024 elections; diplomat; moderate; continued China relationship but less confrontational; RAMSI legacy management

head_of_state.name: King Charles III
head_of_state.title: King of Solomon Islands
head_of_state.notes: Constitutional monarch; represented by Governor-General David Vunagi (since 2019); republic aspirations low

former_leaders.name: Manasseh Sogavare
former_leaders.notes: Four-time PM; switched recognition to China 2019 (triggered riots 2021, Malaita opposition); authoritarian tendencies (delayed elections, Hong Kong-style foreign agents bill); Australian/US distrust; Chinese security pact 2022 (alarmed West); polarising; dominant figure 2000s-2020s

former_leaders.name: Allan Kemakeza
former_leaders.notes: PAP; PM during worst of Tensions/civil war; invited RAMSI 2003 (critical decision, saved state from collapse); militia connections

former_leaders.name: Bartholomew Ulufa'alu
former_leaders.notes: Liberal Party; ethnically Malaitan; ousted by coup June 2000 (MEF-backed, held at gunpoint); economic reformer; tragic victim of ethnic politics

former_leaders.name: Sir Peter Kenilorea
former_leaders.notes: First PM at independence; built nation from scratch; respected statesman; founding father; SIAC; died 2016
